/-!
# Conjecture 8.85

by E. I. Khukhro

Construct a finite $p$-group $G$ whose Hughes subgroup
$H_p(G) = \langle x \in G \mid |x| \ne p \rangle$ is non-trivial and has index $p^3$.

The Hughes subgroup $H_p(G)$ of a group $G$ is the subgroup generated by the elements of
order different from $p$. The Hughes conjecture asserted that if $H_p(G)$ is a proper
non-trivial subgroup of a finite $p$-group $G$, then it has index $p$. G. E. Wall found a
counterexample for $p = 5$ in which $H_p(G)$ has index $p^2$. The problem asks for an
example in which the index is $p^3$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

def hughesSubgroup (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure {x : G | orderOf x ≠ p}
blocks.docstring:
The Hughes subgroup $H_p(G) = \langle x \in G \mid |x| \ne p \rangle$ of a group $G$:
the subgroup generated by all elements of $G$ whose order is not $p$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Subgroup.closure applied inline to {x | orderOf x ≠ p}; also considered Mathlib's exponent/omega-subgroup style notions (Subgroup.zpowers, Monoid.exponent), none of which capture the subgroup generated by elements of order ≠ p.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.85».hughesSubgroup
justification.why_needed: The Hughes subgroup H_p(G) = ⟨x ∈ G | |x| ≠ p⟩ has no counterpart in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (rg for 'hughes' only hits author names in ring-theory files). Defined as Subgroup.closure {x : G | orderOf x ≠ p}.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem hughesSubgroup_normal (p : ℕ) : (hughesSubgroup p G).Normal where
  conj_mem n hn g := by
    have h : (hughesSubgroup p G).map (MulAut.conj g).toMonoidHom ≤ hughesSubgroup p G := by
      rw [Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap, hughesSubgroup, Subgroup.closure_le]
      intro x hx
      apply mem_hughesSubgroup_of_orderOf_ne
      have hord := orderOf_injective (MulAut.conj g).toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj g).injective x
      simpa using hord.trans_ne hx
    exact h (Subgroup.mem_map_of_mem _ hn)
blocks.docstring: The Hughes subgroup is a normal subgroup.

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem hughesSubgroup_multiplicative_zmod_eq_bot (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] :
    hughesSubgroup p (Multiplicative (ZMod p)) = ⊥ := by
  rw [hughesSubgroup, Subgroup.closure_eq_bot_iff]
  intro x hx
  have h : orderOf x ∣ p := by
    simpa [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, ZMod.card] using
      orderOf_dvd_natCard (G := Multiplicative (ZMod p)) x
  rcases (Nat.dvd_prime hp.out).1 h with h1 | h1
  · exact orderOf_eq_one_iff.1 h1
  · exact absurd h1 hx
blocks.docstring:
In a cyclic group of prime order $p$, every non-identity element has order $p$, so the
Hughes subgroup is trivial.

claims.decomposer_note: Although phrased as 'construct', the content is the existence Prop ∃ prime p, ∃ finite p-group G with H_p(G) := ⟨x : orderOf x ≠ p⟩ ≠ ⊥ and H_p(G).index = p^3; p is implicitly a prime quantified existentially (not 'for every p' — p = 2, 3 are impossible since the Hughes conjecture holds there), Hughes subgroup is the subgroup generated (Subgroup.closure) by elements of order ≠ p (identity included harmlessly), 'non-trivial' means ≠ ⊥, and index p^3 automatically makes it proper.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the identical, faithful proposition: ∃ prime p, ∃ finite group G with IsPGroup p G, Subgroup.closure {x | orderOf x ≠ p} ≠ ⊥ and index = p^3. c04 chosen as base because it names the Hughes subgroup as a bespoke definition `hughesSubgroup` (clearer statement, per CONTRIBUTING's bespoke-definition rule) and supplies the best proven API tests (membership, normality via orderOf_injective, and H_p = ⊥ for the cyclic group of order p, which genuinely tests the definition). I added c01's `hughesSubgroup_eq_top` API lemma and tightened the module docstring. Statement compiled with only the `sorry` warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.85

by E. I. Khukhro

Construct a finite $p$-group $G$ whose Hughes subgroup
$H_p(G) = \langle x \in G \mid |x| \ne p \rangle$ is non-trivial and has index $p^3$.

The Hughes subgroup $H_p(G)$ of a group $G$ is the subgroup generated by the elements of
order different from $p$. The Hughes conjecture asserted that if $H_p(G)$ is a proper
non-trivial subgroup of a finite $p$-group $G$, then it has index $p$. G. E. Wall found a
counterexample for $p = 5$ in which $H_p(G)$ has index $p^2$. The problem asks for an
example in which the index is $p^3$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.85»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- The Hughes subgroup $H_p(G) = \langle x \in G \mid |x| \ne p \rangle$ of a group $G$:
the subgroup generated by all elements of $G$ whose order is not $p$. -/
def hughesSubgroup (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure {x : G | orderOf x ≠ p}

/-- Elements of order different from $p$ lie in the Hughes subgroup. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem mem_hughesSubgroup_of_orderOf_ne {p : ℕ} {x : G} (hx : orderOf x ≠ p) :
    x ∈ hughesSubgroup p G :=
  Subgroup.subset_closure hx

/-- If $G$ has no element of order $p$, then $H_p(G) = G$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem hughesSubgroup_eq_top {p : ℕ} (h : ∀ x : G, orderOf x ≠ p) :
    hughesSubgroup p G = ⊤ :=
  Subgroup.eq_top_iff' _ |>.2 fun x => mem_hughesSubgroup_of_orderOf_ne (h x)

/-- The Hughes subgroup is a normal subgroup. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem hughesSubgroup_normal (p : ℕ) : (hughesSubgroup p G).Normal where
  conj_mem n hn g := by
    have h : (hughesSubgroup p G).map (MulAut.conj g).toMonoidHom ≤ hughesSubgroup p G := by
      rw [Subgroup.map_le_iff_le_comap, hughesSubgroup, Subgroup.closure_le]
      intro x hx
      apply mem_hughesSubgroup_of_orderOf_ne
      have hord := orderOf_injective (MulAut.conj g).toMonoidHom (MulAut.conj g).injective x
      simpa using hord.trans_ne hx
    exact h (Subgroup.mem_map_of_mem _ hn)

/-- In a cyclic group of prime order $p$, every non-identity element has order $p$, so the
Hughes subgroup is trivial. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem hughesSubgroup_multiplicative_zmod_eq_bot (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] :
    hughesSubgroup p (Multiplicative (ZMod p)) = ⊥ := by
  rw [hughesSubgroup, Subgroup.closure_eq_bot_iff]
  intro x hx
  have h : orderOf x ∣ p := by
    simpa [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, ZMod.card] using
      orderOf_dvd_natCard (G := Multiplicative (ZMod p)) x
  rcases (Nat.dvd_prime hp.out).1 h with h1 | h1
  · exact orderOf_eq_one_iff.1 h1
  · exact absurd h1 hx

/--
Construct a finite $p$-group $G$ whose Hughes subgroup
$H_p(G) = \langle x \in G \mid |x| \ne p \rangle$ is non-trivial and has index $p^3$.

This is stated as the existence of a prime $p$ and a finite $p$-group $G$ with
$H_p(G) \ne 1$ and $|G : H_p(G)| = p^3$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.85» :
    ∃ (p : ℕ) (_ : p.Prime) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (_ : Finite G),
      IsPGroup p G ∧ hughesSubgroup p G ≠ ⊥ ∧ (hughesSubgroup p G).index = p ^ 3 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.85»

items: 'Construct …' is formalized as a plain existence Prop (no answer(sorry) ↔), following the decomposition table's note; if the problem were shown impossible the repo convention would negate the statement.
p is quantified existentially as a prime (p.Prime), not universally; per the table's note the problem is not 'for every p'.
Finite p-group encoded as (G : Type) with [Group G], Finite G and IsPGroup p G (the idiom used in Kourovka/20_76.lean); with p prime and G finite this is equivalent to |G| being a power of p.
Element order uses orderOf; the identity (order 1 ≠ p) is a generator of the closure, which does not change the subgroup.
'Non-trivial' is hughesSubgroup p G ≠ ⊥; 'has index p^3' is Subgroup.index = p ^ 3 in ℕ, which is the genuine index since G is finite, and automatically forces H_p(G) to be proper.
Module docstring includes a short historical remark (Hughes conjecture; Wall's 1967 counterexample with index p^2 for p = 5) — a reviewer may wish to check the attribution.

reviewer_notes: Modeling: the imperative 'Construct ...' is rendered as a plain existence Prop (no answer(sorry)), per CONTRIBUTING.md for non-question problems. p is existentially quantified as a prime (the notebook fixes no p; a universal reading would be false since the Hughes conjecture holds for p = 2, 3). 'Finite p-group' = Finite G ∧ IsPGroup p G with p.Prime. Hughes subgroup = Subgroup.closure {x | orderOf x ≠ p} (identity of order 1 is a generator, harmless; orderOf is never 0 in a finite group). Non-trivial = ≠ ⊥; index p^3 uses Subgroup.index, which is the genuine index for finite G and forces properness. Boundary cases checked: trivial group has index 1 ≠ p^3; non-prime p excluded. The bespoke `hughesSubgroup` is generic and could be moved to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/ in a real PR; it is kept in the problem file here because the deliverable is a single file. Module docstring includes brief history (Hughes conjecture; Wall's index-p^2 counterexample for p = 5), which reviewers may verify or trim. No candidate omitted the slot; no decomposition objections were raised and I share none.
